## Ecosystem notes (2026-09-08, updated as research completes)

- Storm season timing: late summer hail/storm damage drives roofing, gutter, siding, and tree care demand in the Denver metro. Roofers and arborists are in their busiest quarter.
- HVAC shoulder season: September is the heating-to-cooling transition; furnace tune-up and replacement campaigns start. HVAC shops see high inbound quote volume.
- Landscaping slowdown: fall cleanup season begins; lawn care inbound softens as winter approaches, but snow removal contracts are being signed now.
- Cleaning/maid services: steady year-round demand; small owner-led teams lose bookings when all cleaners are on jobs.
- Snow/winter services (round 123, 2026-09-23): independent pool nearly exhausted in corridor; 1 fresh qualifier (Grand Junction Landscaping, form-route WATCH). CMP Solutions LLC (Montrose, pipeline round 87, route UNKNOWN) is running a live limited-spots 2026-2027 winter campaign on Instagram (2026-09-04), the strongest current seasonal signal in the segment, but still publishes no own-site contact. SEO farms (thesnowremovalcompany.com, snowremoval-colorado.com, kandmlandscapes.com) and directory-only shops dominate the search surface; genuine independents are mostly landscape/property-service hybrids and phone-first.
- Pattern: the most contactable prospects are owner-led shops with 1-20 employees whose websites show a simple contact form or published email. Larger franchises often route through corporate quote wizards with required property addresses, which blocks honest outreach.
- Common skip reasons to log, not re-add: image CAPTCHA, required property address/ZIP on quote forms, required service-selection checkboxes with no honest answer for B2B outreach, inactive/parked sites.
- Roofing/gutters (batch 1, 17 candidates): Denver sits in Hail Alley; May-Aug hail events create sharp inbound spikes. Nearly every roofer runs a free-inspection program and offers insurance-claim assistance, so a missed call converts directly into a lost insurance claim for a competitor. Gutter market splits between true owner-operators (phone-only or phone-plus-form, cleanest AI concierge fit) and larger local teams that already advertise sub-hour response and would buy speed as a competitive edge. Almost every business leads with a phone number and puts email or form second.
- Plumbing (batch 1, 8 candidates): crowded market of small family shops competing on same-day and 24/7 emergency positioning; almost all run thin websites with phone as the primary inbound route, so after-hours speed decides burst-pipe and sewer calls. Septic/well/pump (batch 1, 10 candidates): cluster on the metro fringe (Castle Rock, Evergreen, Golden, Sedalia), multi-generation families with owner-led dispatch; demand driven by two sharp triggers, septic inspections tied to real-estate closing deadlines and no-water emergencies. Contactability is phone-first in both trades, with only a minority publishing emails or forms.
- HVAC (batch 1, 11 candidates): September heating-season ramp-up with the first cold snap driving a furnace repair and tune-up surge small shops cannot staff phones for. Highly fragmented, dozens of similar family-owned shops all competing on "24/7 emergency, family-owned, fast response", so the differentiator is simply who answers first. Contact routes skew heavily phone-first; many small shops publish no email and bury their quote forms.
- Electrical/solar (batch 1, 16 candidates): electrical shops lean heavily on emergency positioning with 24/7 promises and same-day service, so after-hours missed calls are the clearest pain point; several are expanding services (plumbing, solar wiring), which multiplies inbound volume. Solar is crowded and consultative, competing on batteries, EV chargers, hail repair, and detach/reinstall work; many funnel everything through phone numbers or quote wizards with weak follow-up promises, making missed-call capture and fast lead triage highly relevant.
- Cleaning trades (batch 2, 21 candidates: 9 house cleaning, 11 carpet). House cleaning is dense and competitive: scrappy independents plus franchisees (MaidPro, Merry Maids, Maid Right), almost all running quote wizards or phone-first booking while advertising fast same-day responsiveness, so a missed call or slow quote follow-up is a direct booking loss. Carpet/upholstery skews even more owner-operator: most are one-phone-line trucks with no email, no form, or a bare form; demand spikes around move-outs, pet messes, and floods, so the highest-value, most urgent calls arrive exactly when the owner is elbow-deep in a job and cannot answer.
- Landscaping/snow (batch 1, 16 candidates): overwhelmingly owner-led and phone-first; several established shops have no website at all. Fall cleanup and aeration season is peaking now, and snow contract sign-ups run September through November, so both trades are entering their highest inbound volume window at once. Strongest pattern: the owner doing double duty as estimator, crew chief, and receptionist.
- Insulation/pool/spa (batch 3, 17 candidates: 8 insulation, 9 pool/spa). Denver insulation is a crowded, rebate-driven market where nearly every small shop competes on free estimates and Xcel rebate paperwork, creating high inbound quote volume while owners and crews are on ladders or in attics; several reviews literally mention competitors never calling back. Pool/spa is thinner and more fragmented, a mix of franchise systems and true owner-operators, with year-round hot tub culture (weekly water care, Airbnb rentals, winter freeze repairs), so recurring-route operators miss urgent repair calls while driving routes. Both trades lean heavily on phone-first contact pages with few published emails.
- Movers (batch 3, 13 candidates). Denver metro moving is a crowded, quote-driven market in late peak season, with dozens of small owner-led shops (1-10 people, hourly pricing) competing against national franchises. Most run their whole sales pipeline through a phone line and an online quote form with no dedicated office staff; many publish only a phone number, so after-hours and mid-job calls go to voicemail.
- Tree care/windows (batch 3, 16 candidates: 8 tree, 8 window). Tree care is fragmented into small owner-led ISA-certified shops, many selling 24/7 emergency and storm response yet publishing only a phone number; spring storm season and the arrival of emerald ash borer are driving call spikes these teams cannot catch from a bucket truck. Window cleaning skews toward small family operations competing on speed of quote, several already running instant-quote widgets or same-day quote promises they struggle to honor while on ladders, and franchises layering national-brand call volume onto tiny local offices.
- Pest control/chimney (batch 2, 16 candidates: 8 pest, 8 chimney). Pest control is crowded with small locally or family owned shops (1-20 staff) competing against big regional brands, relying on same-day service promises and phone-driven quoting with thin office staffing, which makes missed calls the number one leak. Chimney sweeps are hyper-seasonal with demand compressed into September through November, so even good small crews get buried in a short window and after-hours or mid-job callers vanish. Most own-site contact forms exist but published emails are rare; a meaningful share are effectively phone-only. Note: EnviroPest (Englewood) is likely 50+ employees, above the ideal 1-20 profile, flagged as such.
- Garage doors/locksmiths (batch 2, 16 candidates: 8 garage, 8 locksmiths). Same pattern across both: small owner-led or family-owned shops whose entire growth engine is the phone, leaning heavily on 24/7 emergency and same-day promises. Garage door demand spikes on broken springs, off-track doors, opener failures, and weather shifts; locksmith demand is even more perishable because a locked-out caller simply dials the next company. Very few publish an email or a real contact form, and almost none name an owner or team size, making rapid intake and follow-up the obvious weak point.
- Siding/exteriors/decks (batch 5, 9 candidates, 2026-09-09): new segment. Owner-led exterior shops where estimators double as crew leads; free-estimate funnels and storm-surge inquiries compete with long on-site installs, so follow-up is the leak. Two published emails found (DeckTec, GS Exterior Experts email redacted as placeholder); rest are form/phone-first.
- Junk removal/hauling (batch 5, 10 candidates, 2026-09-09): new segment. Same-day/next-day booking is the whole product and runs on phone and text; most are tiny owner-led crews (one is literally one person), so missed calls during jobs are instant lost revenue. Three site-published emails (Super Junkers, Gone For Good, Pride N Service); rest are booking-widget or phone-first. Note: Buffalo's Construction & Landscaping (Facebook pipeline) lists junk haul-off, keep them under Facebook rather than duplicating here.
- Painting/pressure washing (batch 2, 21 candidates: 10 painting, 11 pressure washing). Painting demand is highly seasonal with peak exterior work roughly May through September; pressure washing is weather-sensitive and often bundled with windows, gutters, painting prep, or property-sale cleanup. Painting companies generally publish emails or estimate forms and can be reached directly, while smaller pressure-washing operators frequently rely on phone calls or quote widgets, making fast lead capture and follow-up the biggest lever for both. Note: Wash On Wheels (Englewood) excluded as too large at roughly 34 employees; Show Me Pressure Washing excluded as a Tennessee SEO site.
- Water damage restoration (batch 4, 10 candidates, 2026-09-08): new segment. Double seasonal peak, spring snowmelt/summer storms plus winter pipe bursts; nearly every shop sells 24/7 emergency response with 60-minute arrival claims, so flood-crisis callers work down a Google list until someone answers. Extremely phone-first segment, few published emails, forms plus phone are the main routes. Fragmented independents (Abbotts, RestoreCo, Restoration Logistics, AquaRescue) handle insurance claims directly, so paperwork drag is a real pitch angle. 4 of 10 are phone-only with unverified numbers from directory listings; treat those as softer candidates.
- Concrete/fencing (batch 2, 16 candidates: 8 concrete, 8 fencing). Concrete shops run phone-first out of necessity: crews are pouring or traveling, several sites have incomplete or broken estimate forms (Caliber 1, Denver Concrete Company), and owners cover wide territories with appointment-based quoting. Fencing firms compete across cedar, vinyl, composite, chain-link, steel, gates, and repairs, where estimate requests involve property details, site visits, permits, and financing questions spread over multiple team members. Across both trades the pattern is the same: homeowners collect several bids, missed calls are invisible, and the shops that respond first win the job.
- Appliance/handyman (batch 3, 21 candidates: 11 appliance, 10 handyman). Appliance repair is urgency-driven: same-day or next-day service, one to three hour arrival windows, phone-first booking; inbound calls arrive hot and a missed ring sends the customer to a competitor. Handyman businesses run on variety: project photos, estimates, and multi-trade job types require qualification and scheduling before dispatch, so their pain is sorting and follow-up rather than pure speed. Both trades are owner-led small teams with little or no office staff; only a handful publish a general email, and owner names are rarely stated, so outreach should lean on personalized angles tied to their posted promises rather than naming decision-makers.
- Flooring/remodeling (batch 3, 17 candidates: 9 flooring, 8 remodeling). Flooring leads run on free in-home estimates and mobile showroom visits, so prospects cluster around homeowners waiting for someone to show up with samples; refinishing crews work in occupied homes where missed calls are easy. Remodelers rely on consultation forms or direct owner phone lines for high-ticket kitchen, bath, addition, and whole-home projects, so the fit is fast intake and qualification while the owner is on a job site. Few publish direct emails and several use appointment or quote wizards.
- Painting/pressure washing (batch 2, 21 candidates: 10 painting, 11 pressure washing). Painting demand is highly seasonal with peak exterior work roughly May through September; pressure washing is weather-sensitive and often bundled with windows, gutters, painting prep, or property-sale cleanup. Painting companies generally publish emails or estimate forms and can be reached directly, while smaller pressure-washing operators frequently rely on phone calls or quote widgets, making fast lead capture and follow-up the biggest lever for both. Note: Wash On Wheels (Englewood) excluded as too large at roughly 34 employees; Show Me Pressure Washing excluded as a Tennessee SEO site.

- Irrigation & sprinkler (batch 1, 11 candidates, 2026-09-09): new segment. Mid-September is the ramp-up to Denver's winterization season (average first hard freeze around October 8, blowout window roughly late September through mid-November); multiple shops warn October appointments fill fast. Pricing observed on company sites runs $85 flat (Mile Hi Services, multi-trade, excluded) to $150 per blowout (Sprinkler Doctor), a high-margin, high-volume, short-window service. Shops skew heavily owner-operator or small family crews (Conrad Olivier at 5280 Sprinklers, Hawkins Brothers, Dave Ferdon's Thornton Sprinklers) who answer their own phones while in the field, the perfect missed-call pain profile: a homeowner who gets voicemail during a freeze warning books the next name on the list, and the shop loses both the blowout and the spring startup. Several shops already push text-first or online booking (303 Sprinklers, 5280 Sprinklers, Sprinkler Doctor), signaling they feel inbound strain. Skip patterns logged: national franchises (Conserva Irrigation), multi-trade companies where blowouts are a side offering (Mile Hi Services, Omni Landscape, Denver Lawn & Snow Care), fire-suppression sprinkler companies (Denver Fire Pro), and directory-only operations with no real site (Gorman's Sprinklers Too, KHEN Sprinklers). Verification caveats kept: Thornton "Sprinklers" (Dave Ferdon) dropped entirely, no own site found; Preferred Sprinklers recorded as form-route only since its directory phone never appeared on its own site.
- Kitchen & bath / countertops (batch 1, 13 candidates, 2026-09-09): new segment, kept distinct from the earlier general-remodeler batch. Segment is consult-driven high-ticket sales: free in-home estimates, design consultations, showroom appointments, laser measurements. Most shops are small family crews who live on the tools and cannot answer mid-install. Mid-September is a fall planning window: homeowners want work scheduled before the holidays, contractors want pipelines filled before winter. BathHound was actively advertising 50% off installation and locked 2026 pricing, pointing to live lead capture and price-sensitive comparison shopping. Contact routes skew phone-plus-email; one owner explicitly published (Sarah Ocasek at Blackbird Kitchen and Bath). Excluded per segment rules: Re-Bath Denver (franchise), Northbuilt Construction (general remodeler), Thurston Kitchen + Bath (cabinet/appliance showroom with no install-crew evidence), Coronado Bath and Tile (unreliable contact info). Near-misses needing one more own-site check if the pipeline needs topping up: Kitchen Masters (Lakewood), C & C Kitchens (Denver), 5280 Stone Company (Frederick).
---

- Foundation/masonry/drywall (batch 7, 25 candidates, 2026-09-09): new segments. Foundation repair & basement/crawlspace waterproofing (6 candidates): Mid-September 2026 is prime inspection season in Denver metro: monsoon rains and summer watering have swollen the area's expansive clay soils, so homeowners are discovering seepage, wall cracks, bowing basement walls, and drainage failures right as the pre-freeze window opens. Foundation and waterproofing jobs are high-ticket and almost always won or lost at first contact, and the owner-led shops here are typically in the field on jobs all day. Segment is clean of national brands in the small-shop tier (Groundworks, Thrasher, Ram Jack dealers all skipped as corporate/franchise). Watch for lead-broker style sites ("our network's experts" copy) that look like contractors but are not. Masonry & stucco (10 candidates): Mid-September 2026 is the last good stretch of Denver's exterior work window, and freeze-thaw season is approaching fast, exactly when homeowners discover cracked stucco, failing tuckpointing, and leaky chimney crowns, driving a rush of repair inquiries. Most shops are family-run crews of one to five people with the owner on the scaffold or at the job site, so incoming calls routinely go to voicemail or get answered after hours. Core pitch fit: AI call capture answers every ring, qualifies the repair, and books the free estimate, while automated follow-up keeps quotes from going cold. Skip pattern: multi-state branded stucco sites and larger remodelers that bundle stucco as one of many trades. Drywall & texture (9 candidates): September is the pivot point in Colorado as exterior work winds down and homeowners turn to basements, texture re-dos, popcorn ceiling removal, and water-damage repairs, so these shops want to keep crews busy with interior projects. The market is fragmented: dozens of owner-led shops of one to twenty people, most taking intake by phone or a basic contact form, many owners doubling as estimator and scheduler. Strongest fits are owner-operators (Benjamin at B&D Drywall, owner-run Flow Drywall) where every missed call is missed revenue; already-staffed firms are lower priority. Stay excluded: franchise systems (PatchMaster, Hole in the Wall, All Four Walls) whose local operators have less buying authority, plus thin AI-template sites and no-own-site directory-only operations.
- Chimney sweeps (Western CO, 11 candidates, 2026-09-09): September through November is the annual sweep rush (pre-heating-season cleanings, Level I/II inspections, real-estate inspection demand). Shops are small owner-led family crews; the owner is on the ladder or roof mid-job, so inbound calls go to voicemail and after-hours callers book whoever answers first. Phone-first intake with thin office staffing is the norm; credentialed techs whose time is the product lose high-value inspection work across multi-county territories when they miss a ring. Skip patterns: directory-only with no own site, templated multi-city SEO lead-broker pages, phone-only own sites, address-gated quote wizards.
- Handyman (Western CO, 4 candidates, 2026-09-09): fall is the busiest booking window: honey-do lists, deck/fence repairs, gutter cleaning, swamp-cooler winterization before the first hard freeze, heat-cable and pipe protection, holiday-guest prep punch lists. Second-home owners in Aspen/Snowmass/Steamboat send photo-based requests from out of town. Core pain: missed calls and slow estimates while the owner is on a ladder, plus estimate follow-up that dies when the day runs long; photo intake and estimate-chasing are the fit. Market is heavy with phone-only operators, directory-only listings, and dead sites; only own sites with a real email or form qualified.
- Appliance repair (Western CO, 2 candidates, 2026-09-09): urgency-driven, dead-fridge same-day work goes to whoever answers first. Dominated by dealer-service hybrids and family shops on a single phone line; Best Appliance Service (Montrose) publicly booking 2-3 weeks out is the clearest missed-revenue signal seen. Skip patterns: national SEO page farms, corporate, directory/phone-only, Front Range companies with Western CO service pages.
- Fencing (Western CO, 1 candidate, 2026-09-09): late summer/early fall is still build season before the ground freezes; agricultural fence work is a Western Slope staple, mostly owner-built with crews on remote ranch jobs out of cell range. Barrett Fence (GJ) was the one own-site shop with a published email and real form.
- Yield note (2026-09-09): Western CO pools are genuinely thin under the strict own-site email/form rule; ~60 businesses were excluded this run for phone-only, directory-only, dead sites, or lead-broker pages. Future Western CO research will produce small high-quality batches, not big numbers. Flag-worthy near-misses (own sites, no email/form rendered): Best Appliance Service Montrose, Southwest Appliance Durango, Taylor Fence GJ, Valleywide Fence and Deck GJ.
- Plumbing (Western Colorado, batch 13, 2026-09-09): new segment, 2 verified candidates. Shops are overwhelmingly phone-first; smaller independents rarely publish an email or form on their own sites, so the strict own-site rule throttled yield. Mid-September 2026 is shoulder season: irrigation/swamp-cooler work winding down, boiler and heating service about to ramp, second-home and short-term-rental turnover steady in resort markets. Regional players in Montrose and Grand Junction skew family-owned multi-tech with 15-30 years of history; Cortez, Gunnison, Craig, Meeker run thinner with owner-operators.
- HVAC (Western Colorado, batch 13, 2026-09-09): new segment, 10 verified candidates. Independent, family-run, and employee-owned shops rather than national chains, anchored in Grand Junction, Montrose, Glenwood Springs with spokes into Aspen, Basalt, Durango, Hotchkiss, Cortez. September is the hinge month: furnace tune-ups, install-quote follow-up, first-cold-snap breakdowns, plus ski-town second homes needing reliable service from absentee owners. Nearly every shop runs its own site with a working contact form or published email, so direct outreach is practical. Skip patterns: phone-only own sites, parked/dead/hijacked domains, directory-only listings, and a Wheat Ridge-headquartered branch (Major Heating) deprioritized as not clearly local.
- Tree care (Western CO, 11 candidates, 2026-09-10): all four PARTIAL routes resolved 2026-09-10. Rescue Tree Service (Delta), High Country Tree Service (GJ), A, J & G Tree Service (GJ), and Top Notch Trees (GJ) all run customer-only contact forms (free quote / tree service request), no B2B/vendor invitation, so all SKIPPED under the B2B-only form rule, none submitted. Segment note: emerald ash borer is a live Grand Valley demand driver (High Country Tree Service runs EAB content); Top Notch Trees (treeservicegrandjunctionco.com, family-owned since 2018, ISA Certified Arborist, 24/7 emergency) has directory reviews flagging missed calls and answering-service gaps, the clearest missed-call signal in the batch, so flag it for a future email-route retry if an address surfaces. A, J & G Tree Service published phone (970) 200-9425 and address 449 Chuluota Avenue, Grand Junction, CO 81501 but no email.
- Instagram Western CO (9 prospects, 2026-09-10): plumbing, landscape/irrigation, remodel, multi-trade, tree care, and HVAC shops in GJ, Montrose, Durango, Rifle, and Gypsum all publishing emails in bios; all drafted into tailored emails and QUEUED. Notable: James Cook (VIP Plumbing, Durango) is a second-generation Colorado Certified Master Plumber running BlueLight trenchless pipe lining with 24-7 emergency; Littell Electric (Glenwood) is a high-end residential/automation shop where project qualification matters as much as speed.
- Pagosa Springs micro-pool (2026-09-10): thin but real. Yeti Sewer & Drain Solutions (yetidrains.com) is a pre-launch site with only a newsletter signup form, no contact route, stays NEW phone-only; 5280 Plumbing & Drains LLC uses Jobber for online booking (CONFIRMED) but no published email; Sun Ray's Plumbing & Heating name collides with a Long Island, NY company (sunrayservices.com), excluded. Solid Plumbing & Heating (Bayfield/Durango) has directory-published info@solidplumbingdurango.com but the own site shows no email in rendered text, so it stays out of the draft batch pending own-site verification.


- Window cleaning / garage doors (Western Colorado, batch 16, 2026-09-10): only 2 fully verified under the strict own-site rule. Window cleaning enters its fall rush (pre-winter spruce-ups; several shops bundle Christmas light installs, booking starts now). Garage doors are steady year-round with weather-spike demand; shops in this market live on their inboxes more than other trades (Gmail/Yahoo addresses are the norm), so email-first outreach is the natural channel. Grand Junction is densest for window cleaning (6+ own sites), Montrose/Durango for garage doors. Pitch insight: do not lead with "you miss calls" (they know), lead with "your own site already promises speed you cannot deliver without backup." 13 verified near-misses logged in research-scratch-round16.md; one own-site contact-page check each is the highest-yield follow-up (likely 6-10 conversions).
- Snow removal (Western Colorado, batch 15, 2026-09-10): new segment, 5 verified candidates. Mid-September lands squarely in the snow contract-signing window (September through November), the segment's highest-intent inbound period. Own-site evidence documents storm cleanups starting 2-3am with 14-16 hour storm days; storm-morning call chaos, route-capacity pressure, early-hour dispatch, and seasonal contract renewals are the missed-call pain PING targets. Commercial operators with multi-crew routes (D&D Asphalt, Summit Sweeping, Grasshoppers) are the strongest fits. Thinner than expected under the own-site rule; mostly landscaping/asphalt hybrids, phone-primary. If the pool thins, revisit phone-primary near-misses (Peaceful Valley, J&J Snow Removal) or Facebook engagement.
- Roofing (Western Colorado, batch 15, 2026-09-10): new segment, 11 verified candidates. Late-summer hail season winding down but roofers are in their busiest insurance-claim and free-inspection quarter; crews on roofs all day while phones go unanswered, so first-to-answer wins the claim. Coverage concentrated in Montrose (6), Grand Junction (2), Glenwood Springs (2), Durango (1), Gunnison (1); smaller markets yielded only directory/phone-only listings. Pattern: thin WordPress/Squarespace sites where the contact form is the only digital front door; several openly post Gmail/Yahoo addresses, signaling they live in their inboxes. Watch for lookalike regional chains and templated city pages.
- Electrical (Western Colorado, batch 17, 2026-09-10): new segment, 6 verified candidates. September is the pre-heating and pre-winter reliability window: generator evaluations, panel upgrades, service calls, second-home winterization, lighting and shade automation projects, and 24/7 emergency positioning all peak at once. Resort and mountain shops (Steamboat, Glenwood Springs, Durango, Bayfield) sell high-end residential and automation work where qualification and routing matter more than raw lead volume. Owner-led field work with phone/form intake is the norm; pitch reliable capture while electricians are on jobs, not replacing technical judgment. Skip patterns: lead-broker style "electrical network" sites (Duft/Colorado Electrical Network), generic SEO-location pages, and larger multi-tech firms that dilute the owner-led fit (R&A Enterprises included with a size caveat).
- Electrical / septic (Western Colorado, research batch round 31, 2026-09-12): expansion batch, 10 qualified (8 electricians, 2 septic). Own-site emails verified: Hometown Electric (Delta, hometownelectric138@gmail.com, 25+ yrs), Level Up Electric (Cortez, affordableelectricsolutions@gmail.com, rebranded from Hackett, same-day promise), Crested Butte Electrical (oliver@crestedbutteelectrical.com, est. 1978, Skye Houseman, Iron Horse Property Management daily-reliance testimonial, office M-F 8:00-16:30), Southwest Septic (Durango, southwestseptic19@gmail.com, Joe Daulton, Sat hours, Sun closed). Pattern: Gmail intake on basic sites is the norm for small WCO electricians; several sell same-day or emergency positioning with daytime-only offices, giving the after-hours capture angle. Drafts round32-* queued behind round-27 FIFO; cheap-verify Gmail addresses before sending. Note: the JSONL merge for this batch was delayed one run (merged round 32; canonical now 254 rows); legacy free-text enum values across 39 rows normalized to legal enums.
- Duct / dryer vent + commercial janitorial (Western CO, batch 22, 2026-09-10): new segments, 5 verified (3 duct: Advanced Duct Cleaning Durango, Mr. Vac Glenwood/GJ, Rapid Response GJ; 1 janitorial: JP Cleaning Services Glenwood; 1 multi-trade: Timberline Enterprises Gunnison). Duct runs WordPress across all qualifiers, no CRM signals; segment is nearly complete with 2 strong near-misses left (GJ Dryer Vent Cleaning, Quick Draw Cleaning) worth one verification pass on booking/form fields. Janitorial is thin: Elite Cleaning Service (GJ, 70+ employees, commercial-only) is the highest-value next verification target, then Green Space Cleaning and Commercial Cleaners. Segment heat: pre-heating-season is the duct rush window (furnace cleanings, dryer-vent fire-safety calls before winter); janitorial bids and recurring commercial cleanings live or die on response speed.

- Septic / well / pump (Western Colorado, research batch round 23, 2026-09-11): new segment, 9 qualified. Septic pumping runs on 2 to 5 year recall cycles plus emergency demand; several shops promise free estimates and same-day/emergency service, creating the missed-call pain. 24/7 emergency positioning is everywhere but several shops run office-only hours; after-hours calls are the clearest AI receptionist angle. Durango is a septic hot spot (Durango Septic, Mountain Septic, LePew Four Corners, Alpenglow Gunnison). Well and pump shops (San Juan Pump, Valley Pump) have water-outage urgency: a homeowner with no water calls the next shop if the first rings out. Durango Septic literally brands on answering the phone ("the last thing you want is a voicemail") with a small crew in the field. No scheduling software observed anywhere in the segment; software grades UNKNOWN across the board. Segment is nearly all phone-only (8 of 9); only San Juan Pump (Montrose) has an unblocked contact form, though it is a customer form with no B2B invitation.
- Excavation / dirtwork / grading (Western Colorado, research batch round 23, 2026-09-11): new segment, 11 qualified. Demand clusters: site preparation, foundations, grading and drainage, septic installation, utility trenching, demolition, hauling, land clearing. Pitch angles: missed bid requests, estimate follow-up, permit coordination, site-evaluation scheduling, routing residential versus commercial inquiries. Five phone-only operators are most exposed while crews run equipment. Tate Civil (Glenwood) stakes a stated one-business-day inquiry response, a strong speed-to-lead angle. Metcalf (Parachute) runs seasonal intake (spring/summer reclamation and stormwater, fall/winter road and emergency ops). Software: Wix x2, WordPress, GoDaddy x2 CONFIRMED (site platform only); no booking widgets or CRM badges anywhere; rest UNKNOWN. Earthworx (Montrose) has an unblocked customer contact form; Aspen Digger and Miles Rippy have real contact pages.
- Near-miss flags for future segments (all own sites verified 2026-09-11): Forest Scapes LLC (Durango, tree service, forestscapesdurango.com) and Quala-Tree Care LLC (Grand Junction area, qualatreecare.com, contact Joshua Baker-Gutierrez, joshb@qualatreecare.com, 970-570-0184 from city licensing records) are tree-care segment candidates; East River Appliance (Gunnison valley, eastriverappliance.com, family-owned domestic appliance repair) is an appliance-repair candidate. Environmental Excavation LLC (Carbondale, environmentalexcavationllc.com, Squarespace, founders Peter and Alexandra Blake stated) fits excavation but no phone/email/form rendered in fetches; needs one live-browser contact-page check before qualifying.

- Asphalt / paving (Western Colorado, research batch round 24, 2026-09-11): new segment, 8 qualified. September is the tail of Colorado's paving season (May through October); sealcoat needs sustained pavement temps above 50F, so HOA and commercial lot rush before winter is the urgent demand trigger. Crews are on pavers, rollers, and sealcoat rigs all day and cannot answer; estimate follow-up is the pitch. Grand Junction is crowded; Glenwood/Rifle/Carbondale and Durango/Cortez/Pagosa coverage is thinner; Cortez, Pagosa Springs, Craig, and Meeker produced no own-site-verified shops. Software UNKNOWN across all 17 researched; no booking widgets or CRM badges anywhere. Skip patterns: franchise systems (Jet-Black), white-label template farms (Animas Asphalt's "CPS" copy), out-of-state bases. Several strong local shops have weak or no websites (Kauffman, High Country, JB's, CM Asphalt), which is both a pipeline gap and an inbound angle: thin web presence correlates with phone-only workflows and high missed-call pain.
- Garage doors (Denver metro, research batch round 24, 2026-09-11): new segment (outward expansion), 9 qualified. Broken torsion springs are the single most urgent trigger; a door stuck open is a security emergency. Several shops advertise 24/7 but run daytime-only offices, so after-hours missed-call capture is the clean pitch. Segment is saturated with templated city-page SEO farms and a national franchise layer (A1, Precision, Dave's); Colorado-ownership verification stays mandatory. Watch address-sharing brands (A1 Garage Door Service shares 5081 Kingston St with Don's Garage Door Repair). Shops show little evidence of Housecall Pro style booking wizards; most routes are plain phone numbers or simple WordPress forms, so lead with missed-call capture rather than booking-friction relief. 7 Denver-area near-misses (Arvada Garage Door, AVI, Incredible, Mile High Sales & Repair, Garage Door Knights, DMAC, Gold Label Door) are BBB-listed with no own website; qualify on own-site discovery.
- Solar installers (Western Colorado, research batch round 25, 2026-09-11): new segment, 9 qualified. Richest new Western Slope segment this round. Federal tax credits expired 12/31/2025 (stated on Solar Design Group's own site), so every remaining lead costs more to win, which is the core capture/follow-up argument. Shops are small, consultative, permit-heavy: utility usage analysis, permits, interconnection, net metering, PTO, monitoring-app handoff (Atlasta); rebate paperwork for GEO and LPEA (Durango Solar Works); 4CORE Home Upgrade program network creates rebate-paperwork load in the southwest. Orphaned-system repair is a real sub-market (Sunsense markets rescue of systems installed by other firms; Shaw and High Noon sell maintenance contracts). Software UNKNOWN across all; no Aurora/OpenSolar/Sighten/Snugg Pro, no CRM or booking widgets anywhere. Skip patterns: regional multi-state operators (Big Dog Solar), parked domains (Four Corners Solar), national location pages, placeholder-data sites (SoL Energy).
- Insulation (Western Colorado, research batch round 25, 2026-09-11): new segment, 1 qualified (Eagle Insulation, Durango, robert@eagleinsulationco.com). Pool is genuinely thin under the own-site rule: 11 near-misses logged, most established GJ firms are phone-only own sites or directory-only. Durango/Pagosa spray foam scene is tied to mountain-town winterization and second-home work; 4CORE preferred-contractor list is the pressure point (rebate and energy-efficiency questions create qualification load). Seasonal timing favorable (mid-September pre-heating-season weatherization rush). Pitch: field-heavy crews publish same-day or 24-hour callback promises; instant-response lead capture is the concrete angle. Expect future insulation batches to stay small.
- Flooring / hardwood / tile (Western Colorado, research batch round 25, 2026-09-11): substitute segment, 3 qualified. Dealer-network showrooms dominate (Carpets Plus Flooring America affiliates); independent install shops are phone-only heavy (The Flooring Guy Durango, Home Roots Hardwood Flooring Durango, Yanon's Montrose). Mid-September is the pre-winter install window in mountain towns: second-home owners rushing projects before ski season, short-term rental turnovers. Pitch: free in-home estimate requests that die unanswered while crews sand floors; out-of-town second-home owner coordination. NWFA/Bona certifications are common trust signals. QuickBooks CONFIRMED at Renwick Tiles (already covered in playbook); no CRM/booking/estimating software anywhere in the batch.
- Siding / exteriors / decks & outdoor living (Western Colorado, round 42, 2026-09-13): brand-new WCO segment. The pipeline covered WCO roofing, concrete, and fencing but never siding or deck specialists. Discovery leaned on GJ vinyl siding shops and Durango deck builders; Montrose siding work runs through roofing/siding combos with no published own site. Near-misses are concentrated here and one browser fetch failed, so the next pass should be a live on-site contact-route verification before any outreach. Grand Valley Seamless Siding and CL Deck and Porches are the two cleanest segment fits.
- House cleaning / maid services (Western Colorado, round 42, 2026-09-13): brand-new WCO segment; prior house-cleaning work was Denver-metro only, and WCO cleaning coverage stopped at carpet, duct, and commercial janitorial. The segment is rich in small owner-led shops with phone-only listings, which matches the missed-call angle precisely. Elite Cleaning Service (70+ employees, weekly recurring base) is the highest-value target; La Plata Cleaning carries a live missed-inquiry review signal. Franchises (Merry Maids GJ) and broker platforms (Walmart house cleaning, Care.com, Thumbtack, Turno, Homeaglow) were excluded. Sparkling and Beyond RE-VERIFIED from the 2026-09-13 archive (own-site email + phone now confirmed on its FAQ page) but held on WATCH: its site shows TN and IA city pages, so local ownership must be verified before any outreach.
- Epoxy / concrete coatings (Western Colorado, round 55, 2026-09-14): brand-new WCO segment. Independent pool is genuinely thin once chains are removed: national/regional systems (Garage Kings, GarageFloorCoating.com dealer network with pages for nearly every Western Slope town, Spartan Floor Coatings) dominate search visibility. Remaining independents are small owner-operated shops in the northwest and mountain corridors (Craig, Steamboat, Roaring Fork, Pagosa), plus painters for whom epoxy floor coatings are a secondary line (Mountain Sky Closets and Garages, Todd Hill Painting, Sloop Painting). Recurring pattern: phone-only intake, no email/form/follow-up machinery, which is exactly the missed-call opening but only WATCH-grade until verified per business. Pre-winter pitch angle supported by multiple coating sites (garage floor protection against snowmelt, road salts, freeze-thaw), but keep it generic, not personalized, until a business-specific problem is verified. Skip patterns: chain/dealer systems (Garage Kings, GarageFloorCoating.com pages, Spartan), out-of-state SEO location pages (Florida company running a Cortez page), generic lead-gen toll-free pages, athletic-court-only resurfacing, Front Range companies.
- Awning / shade / patio covers (Western Colorado, round 55, 2026-09-14): brand-new WCO segment. Specialist pool is genuinely sparse as of September 2026: two deep specialists verified (Canvas Shade in GJ, third-generation since 1949, structured multi-step intake form, owner named on site, the clearest WARM in the pool; Durango Shade Company, Wix site, motorized shade systems by phone), two Montrose-area owner-operators (Alpine Shades, motorized/smart-home products, phone-only; Colorado Awning and Screen, Eclipse retractable specialist, own site failed to render this round), one GJ retractable-awning specialist (Western Slope Shading Solutions, WordPress, no own-site contact found), one Glenwood contractor (Daybreak, aging site, awning is one service line, revamp candidate). Mid-September timing is tail-end for shade sales season (commercial restaurant patio enclosures and residential shade sails sell hardest in spring/early summer); fall angle is commercial patio enclosure and off-season planning. Skip patterns: interior window-treatment showrooms (Ambassador Blind, Shades Done Right, Budget Blinds, Gotcha Covered = franchises), general deck/fence builders, Front Range companies, national manufacturers, directory/lead-broker pages, tent manufacturers.
